description: Engine API bodies that carry the document format: the session and what the engine supports, the profile list and creating and duplicating profiles, documents, blobs, commits, undo, redo and revert and their results, problems, integration tokens, sensors and their readings, the engine settings, the engine's recent log entries, the displays, the USB panel devices, and the preview socket's messages, frame headers (with item bounds) and change events. spec/openapi.json says which request carries which. See docs/api.md, docs/commit.md and docs/geometry.md.

session.description: GET /api/session: the engine, this run of it and what it supports.

engineBuild.description: The source revision the engine was built from, for a bug report (docs/api.md#session): the commit's abbreviated id as git writes it, such as "004cf52", followed by "-dirty" when the build had changes not yet committed; "unknown" when the build couldn't tell (built without git or outside a repository, as from a source archive). A client shows it as given.

protocol.description: The engine API's version: 2 for the API these schemas describe. It goes up only when the API changes in a way a client can't ignore (a member or endpoint removed or changed); members and endpoints are added without changing it.

instance.description: This run of the engine: new every time the engine starts, so a client that sees another knows the engine restarted (and that every document tag it read before is stale). Not a document's tag: a commit names its document's (documentResponse).

started.description: When this run of the engine started, in UTC to the second. The same for the whole run, like `instance`.

features.description: The optional API features the engine has, by name, each once (docs/api.md#session): every operation added after this version of the API comes under one, and a client uses it only when its name is listed. This version defines `plugins` (the requests under /api/plugins and POST /api/folders/plugins/open, docs/api.md#plugins), which an engine lists whether or not it hosts plugins, `devices` (the requests under /api/devices and the socket's `devices` message, docs/api.md#devices), which an engine lists whether or not it drives panels, `simulated.text` (a `simulated` subscription makes up text and tables as well as numbers, docs/api.md#simulated-sensors), and `sensors.image` (GET /api/sensors/image, an image sensor's picture, docs/api.md#sensor-pictures). A client ignores a name it doesn't know.

platform.description: The operating system the engine runs on. A client treats a platform it doesn't know as `other`.

osVersion.description: The operating system's version as it reports it, for a bug report: on macOS its product version ("26.1", "15.6.1"), on Windows major.minor.build ("10.0.26100"), on Linux the kernel release ("6.8.0-45-generic"); "unknown" when the engine can't read it. Each system writes its own: a client shows it as given.

arch.description: The processor architecture the engine runs as: the engine's own, so an engine emulated on another architecture reports the one it was built for. A client treats an architecture it doesn't know as `other`.

dataDir.description: The folder the engine keeps its data in: an absolute path on the engine's machine.

port.description: The port the engine listens on, on 127.0.0.1 (docs/api.md#session), so a client served from another origin, such as a reverse proxy's on this computer, can name it. The same for the whole run.

mock.description: Whether the engine's sensors aren't the computer's (docs/api.md#session): it runs in mock mode, started to simulate them, or replays a recording of a computer's sensors, so a client can say its readings aren't real. It changes only when the engine restarts.

sessionMedia.description: The media the engine can show beyond stored assets (docs/api.md#session): `providers`, the media providers configured on it by name (docs/providers.md), each once. A scene's provider source names one of them; `media.provider` in the scene format's capabilities says only that providers exist. It changes only when the engine restarts.

providers.description: Provider names, as a provider source's `provider` is written (`http`: web images; `now-playing`: the cover of what the computer plays; `rtsp`: camera streams, listed only by an engine that can decode video). A client ignores a name it doesn't know.

sessionLocale.description: The PC's regional format as the engine read it when it started (docs/api.md#session): a profile without a `locale` draws numbers and dates with it, and a client that formats readings of its own uses it so they match the frames. It changes only when the engine restarts.

tag.description: Its language and region, such as en-SG; `und` when the engine knows no language for it.

decimalSeparator.description: Written between a number's integer digits and its decimals.

groupSeparator.description: Written between groups of three integer digits.

apiFeature.description: The name of an optional API feature (session.features), written as a capability is: lower-case words joined by dots.

instanceId.description: An opaque id, compared for equality only: a run of the engine (the session's and hello's `instance`), or a document's lifetime tag (a profile entry's, a document response's and a doc event's `instance`, docs/api.md#a-documents-tag), new every time the engine creates or opens the document. A document's revisions belong to its tag.

profileEntry.description: One profile in GET /api/profiles, an array of these in display order, and the 201 answer to creating or duplicating one. `status` says whether the engine can open the profile's document, and which members come with it: ok (name, width, height, rev and dirty), unsupported (it needs a format major version or document capability this engine lacks: a problem, and the name when the document has one) or unreadable (the stored document can't be read, isn't JSON, or breaks the document schema or a document limit outside its scenes: a problem only). Every entry has the document's tag, `instance`, which its DELETE names. An unsupported or unreadable profile is listed and deleted, never opened and never exported (docs/unsupported.md). A client treats a status it doesn't know as a profile it can't open.

profileEntryOk.description: A profile whose document the engine opens. A document with invalid or unsupported scenes is ok: those items are placeholders (docs/unsupported.md).

instance.description: The document's tag: the same as its document response's and doc events'.

dirty.description: The document has changes that aren't saved.

recovered.description: When the document's unsaved changes were kept before the engine last stopped (docs/document.md#revisions): present from the restore until the document is saved or reverted. A client shows it only while `dirty`.

profileEntryUnsupported.description: A profile whose document needs a format major version or a document capability this engine lacks.

instance.description: The profile's tag, new when the engine first reads it in a run: what its DELETE names.

name.description: The document's `profile.name` when that is a string of 1–256 characters, else absent.

problem.description: Why the engine doesn't open it: `unsupported.format` (at /format) or `unsupported.capability` (at /requires/i), with a JSON pointer into the stored document.

profileEntryUnreadable.description: A profile whose stored document can't be read, isn't JSON, or breaks the document schema or a document limit outside its scenes.

instance.description: The profile's tag, new when the engine first reads it in a run: what its DELETE names.

problem.description: The first problem found, with a JSON pointer into the stored document: `io` (the file can't be read), `json` (not JSON) or a document check's code (`schema`, `limit.documentBytes`, ...; docs/validation.md).

profileStatusProblem.description: 409 application/problem+json: the profile's document can't be opened (its status is unsupported or unreadable), so it can't be read, changed, saved, drawn or exported. It can still be listed and deleted.

code.description: The profile's status. A client treats a status it doesn't know as a profile it can't open.

createProfileRequest.description: POST /api/profiles: a new profile under a client-chosen id, either empty (a canvas with no items) or from a document. An id that already exists: 409 existsProblem. Answered 201 with the new profile's profileEntry (docs/api.md).

createProfileEmpty.description: An empty profile: a document with this name and canvas size and no items.

id.description: The new profile's id, chosen by the client.

createProfileFromDocument.description: A profile from a document (importDocument), checked as a stored document is: a scene that is invalid or unsupported (or over a budget) is kept as sent and drawn as a placeholder; a document the engine wouldn't open is refused (422). The document's own `id` (optional; a document id when given) is replaced by `id`, and its `rev` members are ignored.

id.description: The new profile's id, chosen by the client.

importDocument.description: A document (infopanel.document/1) as a create takes it: the document format with its `id` and `rev` members optional (they are ignored: the create's `id` replaces the document's) and every scene taken as stored (storedScene), so a document the engine exported, with scenes it draws as placeholders, can be created again. Its scenes are then checked as a stored document's are (docs/api.md).

id.description: Ignored: the create's `id` replaces it.

items.description: Top-level items in drawing order: the first is at the back.

importSceneItem.description: A scene item as a create takes it (document format: sceneItem), with its scene as stored.

importGroupItem.description: A group item as a create takes it (document format: groupItem).

children.description: In drawing order: the first is at the back.

duplicateProfileRequest.description: POST /api/profiles/{id}/duplicate: a copy of the profile's current document under a client-chosen id. An id that already exists: 409 existsProblem. Answered 201 with the copy's profileEntry.

id.description: The copy's id, chosen by the client.

existsProblem.description: 409 application/problem+json: a profile with the requested id already exists (a create or duplicate whose first attempt succeeded, retried, gets this), or a saved device has the 1.x device id, or the family and serial, a save names (POST /api/devices). Nothing was created.

id.description: For a device (POST /api/devices): the saved device's id (deviceEntry.id), always present. Absent for a profile, whose id the request names.

documentResponse.description: GET /api/profiles/{id}: the profile's current document, with its revision members (the `rev` of the document, the profile and every item), and its state.

instance.description: The document's tag (docs/api.md#a-documents-tag), which these revisions belong to: what its commits, undo, redo, revert and DELETE name, and a save may. Not the session's instance.

rev.description: The document's revision: the same as `document.rev`.

dirty.description: The document differs from the saved one.

recovered.description: When the document's unsaved changes were kept before the engine last stopped (docs/document.md#revisions): present from the restore until the document is saved or reverted. A client shows it only while `dirty`.

responseDocument.description: A document (infopanel.document/1) as the engine returns it: every revision member set, and every scene exactly as stored (storedScene).

items.description: Top-level items in drawing order: the first is at the back.

responseProfile.description: The document's profile, with `rev`: the document revision at which a profile field last changed.

responseSceneItem.description: A scene item as the engine returns it (document format: sceneItem), with its `rev` and its scene as stored.

rev.description: The document revision at which the item last changed.

responseGroupItem.description: A group item as the engine returns it (document format: groupItem), with its `rev`.

rev.description: The document revision at which the item last changed.

children.description: In drawing order: the first is at the back.

storedScene.description: A scene exactly as stored: an object with a string `format`. A scene the engine draws normally matches the scene schema (urn:infopanel:scene:1); one it draws as a placeholder (it needs a newer format or a capability the engine lacks, breaks a rule or limit, or can't be compiled) is returned unchanged and may not (docs/unsupported.md).

blobInfo.description: POST /api/blobs: a stored blob. The engine stores any bytes up to the `videoBytes` limit (more: 413, not stored), named by their SHA-256, and inspects them as a media asset: the answer has `media`, what it found, or `mediaError`, why they can't be used as media (a scene's media naming such a blob draws the missing-media placeholder).

blobInfoMedia.description: A stored blob that is a media asset within the media limits.

id.description: `sha256:` and the SHA-256 of the bytes as sent, in lower-case hex.

bytes.description: The blob's size in bytes: at most `videoBytes` (256 MiB, docs/limits.md); a picture's used as media at most `mediaBytes` (32 MiB).

blobInfoMediaError.description: A stored blob that can't be used as media: not media at all, or media that breaks a media check (a picture over `mediaBytes` included).

id.description: `sha256:` and the SHA-256 of the bytes as sent, in lower-case hex.

bytes.description: The blob's size in bytes: at most `videoBytes` (256 MiB, docs/limits.md); a picture's used as media at most `mediaBytes` (32 MiB).

mediaError.description: Why the bytes can't be used as media: the media check's first error (docs/validation.md: `media.*`, or a `limit.*` code: `limit.mediaBytes` for a picture over 32 MiB, never `limit.videoBytes`, whose bytes aren't stored), with path "".

mediaInfo.description: A media asset as the engine read it from its header or container, without decoding it (docs/validation.md). Sizes are in pixels; an SVG's come from its `width` and `height` or its `viewBox` (docs/svg.md); a video's are its first video track's coded size (docs/smart-nodes.md, video files).

format.description: The asset's format: an image's, or a video's container (`mp4` for mp4 and mov, `matroska` for mkv and webm, `avi`). A client treats a format it doesn't know as it treats the others: media the engine draws.

frames.description: 1 for a still image; an animation's frame count; a video's frame count as its container states it, 1 when it states none.

duration.description: An animation's length in seconds (one loop); 0 for a still image; a video's length as its container states it, 0 when it states none.

codec.description: A video's codec; absent for an image. A client treats a codec it doesn't know as it treats the others: a video the engine plays.

commitRequest.description: POST /api/profiles/{id}/commit. The ops apply in order, all or none, as one undo step (or merged into the previous one, see coalesceKey).

opId.description: Unique per commit, chosen by the client (a UUID, say). Retrying with the same opId and the same body (byte for byte) returns the first result without applying anything again.

instance.description: The tag of the document the client's revisions came from (its documentResponse, profile entry or doc event). Another one (the engine restarted, or the profile was deleted and created again): 409 with reason "instance".

baseRev.description: The document revision the commit is based on: the document `rev` the client last read before it built the commit. It tells a retry from a new commit once the engine has forgotten older opIds: an unknown opId whose baseRev is older than the engine's retry window, or at or below its retry watermark and older than the document's `rev`, is refused (409 expiredProblem; docs/commit.md). Greater than the document's `rev`: 422 (baseRev.future). Each op's own `baseRev` decides its conflicts.

coalesceKey.description: Merge this commit's undo step into the previous one when that had the identical key and the key starts with "gesture:" or less than 1 s passed. A key names one gesture of one client: it includes a random part chosen once per client instance ("gesture:5b0e8f0c-3c1d-4b8e-a7f2-1d9c6e4a2b7f:7").

baseRev.description: The document revision the change is based on: the document `rev` the client last read, for every kind of op (not the item's own `rev`). The op conflicts when a field group it writes (for `remove`, any field of the item or of anything in it) last changed at a revision greater than this. Greater than the document's `rev`: the commit is refused (422, baseRev.future). Absent: no check.

setDesignOp.description: Replaces a scene item's design: layout, source and scene together (absent or null layout or source: none), and its origin when given (null removes it; absent keeps it).

setAttributesOp.description: Sets the given attributes of an item (scene or group); one given as null is removed (docs/commit.md).

insertOp.description: Adds an item (with its children, for a group) to the top level (parentId absent or null) or to a group, at `index` (past the end of the list, or absent: the end, the front).

removeOp.description: Removes an item and everything in it.

moveOp.description: Moves an item to `index` (in the target list once the item has been taken out; past its end: the end) of the top level or a group. Its placement is kept as it is (local coordinates) unless `placement` is given.

itemIndex.description: A position in a list of items, 0 first (at the back). At most 2,000, the document's item limit: a larger value is invalid, never clamped. An index past the end of the list means the end.

opIndex.description: The index of an op in its commit: below 1,000, the op limit.

parentRef.description: A group's item id, or null (or absent) for the top level.

profileOp.description: Sets the given profile fields; each replaces the field whole, and an optional one given as null is removed (docs/commit.md). name, width and height can't be removed.

historyRequest.description: The body of POST /api/profiles/{id}/undo, /redo and /revert, and optionally of /save: the state the client's request is based on. Another document's tag: 409 conflictProblem (reason "instance"); a `baseRev` greater than the document's `rev`: 422 invalidProblem (baseRev.future); a document whose `rev` isn't `baseRev`: 409 conflictProblem (reason "changed"); nothing is done in each case (docs/commit.md).

instance.description: The tag of the document the client's revision came from (its documentResponse, profile entry or doc event).

baseRev.description: The document `rev` the client last read: the request acts only while the document is still at that revision.

commitResult.description: 200 response to a commit, and to undo, redo, revert and save (docs/commit.md).

rev.description: The document's revision after the commit (unchanged when nothing changed).

items.description: The new `rev` of every item the commit (or undo, redo or revert) changed or added.

profileRev.description: The profile's new `rev`, when the commit changed it.

replayed.description: true when this is the stored result of an earlier commit with the same opId.

commitWarning.description: Accepted, but not drawn as written: code "unsupported" (the scene needs a format or capability this engine lacks; it is kept as it is and drawn as a placeholder).

conflictProblem.description: 409 application/problem+json to a commit, undo, redo, revert or save: nothing was applied or saved. The client refetches, rebuilds its change on the current state and sends it again (a commit with a new opId). A DELETE's 409 is deleteConflictProblem.

conflicts.description: A commit's: every conflict found, at least one. An undo's, redo's, revert's or save's: one `instance` conflict, or one `changed` conflict for each item (and for the profile) with a field group changed after its baseRev. That list can be empty: items removed since are not listed, and an undo, redo or revert step may change no field group.

deleteConflictProblem.description: 409 application/problem+json to a DELETE naming another document's tag: nothing was deleted. The client reads the profile again (its entry or its document).

rev.description: The document's current revision. Absent for a profile that can't be opened, which has none.

op.description: The op that conflicts. Absent when the conflict is the whole request's: reason instance, and every conflict of an undo, redo, revert or save.

reason.description: changed: a field group the op writes last changed at a revision greater than the op's baseRev (see `fields`; for `remove`, any field group of the item or of anything in it, each listed with its own `id`); for an undo, redo, revert or save, a field group that changed after its baseRev. missing: the item or parent doesn't exist at that point of the commit. instance: the request names another tag than the document's (the engine restarted, or the profile was deleted and created again, since the client read it). A client treats a reason it doesn't know as it treats every conflict: it refetches and rebuilds its change.

fields.description: The field groups that changed (docs/commit.md): placement, design, bindings, name, visible, locked, position (parent, and index among the siblings present in both versions), children (a group's membership: an item added to it or taken out of it), or a profile field's name.

expiredProblem.description: 409 application/problem+json: the commit's opId isn't one the engine remembers, and its baseRev is older than the engine's retry window, or at or below its retry watermark (the newest baseRev of a forgotten commit) while the document has moved past it, so the engine can't tell whether it is a retry of a commit it applied and has since forgotten. Nothing was applied. The client reads the document, decides whether its change is still needed, and if so commits it again with a new opId and a current baseRev (docs/commit.md).

invalidProblem.description: 422 application/problem+json: the request body (a commit, a create, duplicate, undo, redo, revert or save body, or a document) breaks the format, a rule or a limit; nothing was applied.

errors.description: Every error, at most 100, then, when there were more, one last error with code `more` (path "") counting the rest (docs/validation.md).

path.description: The exact JSON pointer to what the error is about, in what was checked: the request body, or the stored document or blob (docs/versioning.md#error-codes-and-paths).

code.description: A code from docs/limits.md and docs/validation.md (schema, limit.*, ref.*, type.*, ...). A later engine may add codes: a client handles a code it doesn't know by its family, else by the answer's HTTP status (docs/versioning.md#error-codes-and-paths).

message.description: What went wrong, for people: display text, never read by a client.

itemBounds.description: Where an item is drawn this frame, in profile pixels. `frame` is the layout box (automatic dimensions measured), `ink` what the item covers including effects; both are rectangles before rotation, each rotated by `rotation` degrees about its own centre.

problem.description: Set when the item is drawn as a placeholder: unsupported (needs a newer engine), invalid (breaks a rule or limit), budget (over a document or process budget). A client treats a problem it doesn't know as a placeholder whose reason it can't name.

itemMedia.description: Set when media the item shows had a problem in this tick: the first one, as the engine reports it (docs/api.md#frames). The item itself isn't a placeholder: the media is drawn as the missing-media placeholder, or a provider's last good image stays while it says why the newest couldn't be shown.

code.description: `media.loading` (still loading), `media.missing` (an asset that isn't stored, or was refused), `media.provider` (the provider couldn't fetch it, or the reference isn't one it takes), `media.address` (an address the engine may not connect to, docs/providers.md), `media.reach` (an inward address a source marked public-only may not reach, docs/providers.md), `media.budget` (a video past the engine's decode sessions, docs/smart-nodes.md), or the code a fetched answer was refused with (docs/validation.md: `media.format`, `limit.mediaBytes`, ...). A client treats a code it doesn't know as media that can't be shown.

message.description: Why, for people, in English, such as "The server answered 404."; one longer than 1,024 characters is cut, ending in "…".

frameHeader.description: The JSON header of a frame message on /ws (docs/api.md): the document revision and tick the frame was drawn from, its encoding, scale and size, and where every item is.

tick.description: The render tick the frame was drawn from (docs/identity.md). Within one subscription, frames with the same tick were drawn from the same tick snapshot, and tick numbers never go down.

frameId.description: The frame's number: unique within one run of the engine, and greater for a frame rendered later.

encoding.description: How the payload after the header is encoded: `png`, the whole frame as a PNG; `h264`, one H.264 access unit of the subscription's video stream (docs/api.md#video-frames). A subscription gets only the encodings it can ask for.

keyframe.description: On an `h264` frame: whether it decodes on its own. A decoder starts, and after a size change starts again, at a keyframe.

codec.description: On an `h264` keyframe: the codec string `avc1.PPCCLL` (profile, constraint flags and level, in hexadecimal, from the stream's SPS) to configure a decoder with.

description.description: On an `h264` keyframe: the decoder configuration record (avcC, ISO/IEC 14496-15) of the stream from this keyframe on, in base64. Its SPS says the stream never reorders frames.

encoder.description: On an `h264` keyframe: whether the stream from it on is encoded in `hardware` or `software`. A client shows a value it doesn't know as it is.

fallback.description: On a `png` frame of an `h264` subscription: why it isn't video. `encoder.unavailable`: the engine has no working H.264 encoder; `encoder.failed`: its encoders failed or are busy during this subscription; `encoder.size`: the frame is larger than the video size, or no encoder takes its size. A client reads a value it doesn't know as "video unavailable for this frame".

encodeMs.description: The milliseconds from handing the frame's pixels to its encoder to having the encoded frame: for `h264`, copying and encoding, waiting for the encoder included; for `png`, that PNG's encoding (one PNG may serve several subscriptions).

skipped.description: The frames the engine drew for this subscription and didn't send since the last one it sent (dropped before encoding, or replaced by a newer one before it could be sent).

scale.description: Frame pixels per profile pixel: 0.1 or a multiple of 0.25 from 0.25 to 4. The subscription's scale rounded to a step of 0.25, then lowered while the frame would be over 16 Mpx (docs/api.md#frames).

pixelWidth.description: The frame's width in pixels: profileWidth × scale, rounded (docs/api.md#frames). pixelWidth × pixelHeight is at most 16,777,216.

pixelHeight.description: The frame's height in pixels: profileHeight × scale, rounded (docs/api.md#frames).

profileWidth.description: The profile's canvas width at `rev`, in profile pixels.

profileHeight.description: The profile's canvas height at `rev`, in profile pixels.

itemBounds.description: The bounds of every visible item that has bounds, from the same tick as the pixels, in document order: a group before its children (docs/geometry.md). Each id appears once.

docEvent.description: The `doc` message on /ws: the subscribed document's state. Sent when the subscription starts and after every change to the document or its state (a commit, undo, redo, revert or save, from any client). The engine keeps only the latest state to send: a client that falls behind gets the newest, so it may skip revisions, and the last one it gets is always current. It carries no content; the document at that revision is read with GET /api/profiles/{id}.

instance.description: The document's tag, which `rev` belongs to (docs/api.md#a-documents-tag).

dirty.description: The document differs from the saved one.

recovered.description: When the document's unsaved changes were kept before the engine last stopped (docs/document.md#revisions): present from the restore until the document is saved or reverted. A client shows it only while `dirty`.

formatSupport.description: What an engine supports (part of GET /api/session), by format string: every format it reads, each with the newest minor version of it the engine reads, the format's optional capabilities the engine has and the format's limits. A client ignores a format string it doesn't know.

formatString.description: A format string: a format's name and its major version, such as `infopanel.scene/1` (docs/versioning.md).

version.description: The newest minor version of the format the engine reads, such as "1.0"; it reads every earlier one of the same major version.

capabilities.description: The format's optional capabilities the engine has (docs/versioning.md#capabilities-and-requires). A client ignores one it doesn't know.

limits.description: The format's limits, by name (docs/limits.md says which format each belongs to). A client ignores a name it doesn't know.

createTokenRequest.description: POST /api/tokens (the session token only): a new integration token with a name and scopes. Answered 201 with createdToken, the only answer that carries the token's secret (docs/api.md#authentication).

scopes.description: What the token may do: `read`, `edit` or both. `edit` implies `read`, and the token is answered and listed with both.

tokenInfo.description: An integration token, without its secret: GET /api/tokens (the session token only) answers an array of these, oldest first. The session token is never listed.

kind.description: The token's kind: `integration`, the only kind the API creates and lists.

scopes.description: What the token may do: always `read`, and `edit` when it may change profiles, documents and blobs.

lastUsed.description: When the token last authenticated a request, kept to within a minute; absent when it never has.

createdToken.description: 201 to POST /api/tokens: the new token's tokenInfo members and its secret, `token`, which no other answer carries and the engine doesn't keep (it stores only a hash).

token.description: The secret, sent as `Authorization: Bearer {token}` or on /ws like the session token: `ipi_` and 43 base64url characters (256 random bits).

tokenId.description: An integration token's id, used to revoke it (DELETE /api/tokens/{id}): 32 lower-case hex digits. Not a secret.

tokenName.description: A token's name, for people: 1 to 64 letters, digits, spaces, dots, underscores and hyphens, without a space at either end.

items.description: A scope (docs/api.md#authentication). In what the engine sends, a client shows a scope it doesn't know by its name.

timestamp.description: A UTC time to the second (RFC 3339), such as "2026-10-27T09:30:00Z".

pairingId.description: A paired client's id, used to remove its pairing (DELETE /api/pairings/{id}): 32 lower-case hex digits. Not a secret (docs/api.md#pairing).

pairingCode.description: A one-time pairing code: 16 random bytes as 22 base64url characters, usable once within 2 minutes (docs/api.md#pairing).

pairingInfo.description: A paired client, without its secret: GET /api/pairings (the session token only) answers an array of these, oldest first. A pairing another replaced isn't listed (docs/api.md#pairing).

name.description: The client's name, for people, as it gave it when it paired.

lastUsed.description: When the client last proved its pairing, kept to within a minute; absent when it never has.

pairingCodeRequest.description: POST /auth/pairing/code (no token): a one-time code from a link the engine opened, exchanged once for the run's session token and a lasting pairing (pairingGrant). Answered 403 for a code that is unknown, expired or used before (docs/api.md#pairing).

name.description: The client's name, for people, as the pairing is listed.

replaces.description: The pairing the client held before, if any: it is handed over to the new one, which replaces it (docs/api.md#pairing). An id the engine doesn't have changes nothing.

pairingPassRequest.description: POST /auth/pairing/pass (no token): a pass the configured service signed for a client on another computer, exchanged for the run's session token and a lasting pairing (pairingGrant), as a code is, while the `service.pairing` setting is on. Answered 403 pairingPassProblem for a pass the engine refuses (docs/api.md#pairing-through-the-configured-service).

pass.description: The pass as the service gave it: three base64url parts joined by dots (docs/api.md#pairing-through-the-configured-service). A string that isn't one, the empty string included, is refused as `malformed`.

name.description: The client's name, for people, as the pairing is listed.

replaces.description: The pairing the client held before, if any: it is handed over to the new one, which replaces it (docs/api.md#pairing). An id the engine doesn't have changes nothing.

pairingPassProblem.description: 403 application/problem+json to POST /auth/pairing/pass: the pass is refused, and `code` says why in one word, with no other detail (docs/api.md#pairing-through-the-configured-service).

code.description: `off`, the `service.pairing` setting is off; `malformed`, it isn't a pass in its form; `signature`, the service lists no key by its `kid`, or its signature doesn't check; `audience`, it isn't for pairing; `expired`, its time has passed; `host`, it is for another name than the one the request came to, or one not in `proxy.hosts`; `device`, it is for another computer than the one whose credential the engine keeps; `replayed`, it was used before. A client treats a code it doesn't know as a refusal.

createdPairing.description: A new pairing in a pairingGrant: its pairingInfo members and its secret, which no other answer carries. The client keeps the secret and never sends it (docs/api.md#pairing).

secret.description: The pairing secret: 32 random bytes as 43 base64url characters.

pairingGrant.description: 201 to POST /auth/pairing/code and POST /auth/pairing/pass: the run's session token and instance, and the new pairing. `pairing` is absent when the engine can't keep pairings (it couldn't read or write them): the client connects for this run only (docs/api.md#pairing).

token.description: The session token of this run of the engine, sent as `Authorization: Bearer {token}` and on /ws (docs/api.md#authentication).

instance.description: This run of the engine, as the session's `instance`.

issuedPairingCode.description: 201 to POST /api/pairings/codes (the session token only): a one-time code for a client on another computer, which it exchanges once at POST /auth/pairing/code, as a code from a link the engine opened (docs/api.md#pairing).

expires.description: When the code stops being usable, 2 minutes after it was issued (to the second, rounded down).

origins.description: The origins of the clients served from elsewhere that the engine accepts, which may exchange the code from another computer: the engine's own origins and its development origins aren't listed. Empty when it accepts none.

pairingNonce.description: A nonce of the pairing proofs, Np (the client's) or Ne (the engine's): 32 random bytes as 43 base64url characters, new for every challenge (docs/api.md#pairing).

pairingProof.description: A pairing proof, E, C or A: an HMAC-SHA256 as 43 base64url characters (docs/api.md#pairing).

pairingChallengeRequest.description: POST /auth/pairing/challenge (no token): a client that paired asks the engine to prove first that it holds the pairing's secret, over the client's fresh nonce Np. Answered with pairingChallenge, or 404 for a pairing the engine doesn't have (docs/api.md#pairing).

pairingChallenge.description: 200 to POST /auth/pairing/challenge: the engine's nonce Ne and its proof E over Np, Ne and its own listening port. A client checks E over the port it dialled before it sends anything more (docs/api.md#pairing).

nonce.description: Ne, the engine's nonce: the challenge, single use, for 30 seconds.

pairingProofRequest.description: POST /auth/pairing/proof (no token): the client's proof C for a challenge. Answered with pairingSession, or 403, with one text, for any check that fails (docs/api.md#pairing).

nonce.description: Ne, the challenge this proof answers.

pairingSession.description: 200 to POST /auth/pairing/proof: the run's session token and instance, and the engine's proof A over them. A client uses the token only once A checks over the port it dialled (docs/api.md#pairing).

token.description: The session token of this run of the engine (docs/api.md#authentication).

instance.description: This run of the engine, as the session's `instance`.

proof.description: A, over the token's and the instance's UTF-8 bytes.

scopeProblem.description: 403 application/problem+json: the token is valid but lacks the scope the request needs: `read` or `edit`, or `session` for what only the session token may do (signing in, the token endpoints, the engine settings, the configured service, the recent log entries, opening the engine's folders). A missing, unknown or revoked token is answered 401 instead (docs/api.md#authentication).

scope.description: What the request needs. A client shows a scope it doesn't know by its name: the request is refused all the same.

problem.description: application/problem+json (RFC 9457) for an error without a definition of its own: 400 (a query parameter that isn't a whole number, GET /ws without a WebSocket upgrade), 401 (no valid token), 403 (a request from an origin the engine doesn't accept, a pairing code or proof it refuses), 404 (no such profile, blob, token, pairing, folder or endpoint), 405, 409 (paired clients the engine can't read), 413 (a blob over mediaBytes) and 500 (an engine error, a folder the engine couldn't open, or displays it couldn't list). Its members are for people; a client acts on the status (docs/api.md#errors).

type.description: A URI for the kind of error: the HTTP status's section of RFC 9110.

title.description: The HTTP status's reason phrase, such as "Not Found".

sensorEntry.description: One sensor in GET /api/sensors, an array of these: a sensor the engine's sources offer, with the `key` a binding names (docs/bindings.md) and its status now.

key.description: The sensor's key, as a binding's `key` names it. Opaque.

source.description: The id of the source that offers the sensor.

group.description: The group the source lists the sensor in (a device, say), for people.

unit.description: The unit of its values, for people ("°C", "%"); empty when it has none.

status.description: `live` (a current reading), `stale` (a reading older than the source normally updates, the last value kept), `unavailable` (no reading), `denied` (the operating system refused the engine access to the sensor), `simulated` (no source handles the key; the engine simulates it, in mock mode only) or `missing` (the key isn't well formed). A scene input bound to the sensor reads it as docs/bindings.md#status maps it. A client treats a status it doesn't know as no reading.

type.description: The type of value the sensor reads, as a scene input's type names it (docs/bindings.md): `number`, `text` or `table`; or `image`, a picture, named by a reference (its reading's `text`), whose bytes GET /api/sensors/image answers (docs/api.md#sensor-pictures), and which a `text` input reads as its reference; `number` when the engine can't tell. Taken with `status`, from one read. Known without a reading. A client treats a type it doesn't know as `number`.

sensorValue.description: One reading in GET /api/sensors/values, an array of these: every listed sensor (sensorEntry) that has a reading now, in list order. A sensor without one is left out.

now.description: The current value (the last one when the reading is stale). A value that isn't a finite number is 0.

min.description: The lowest value the source has reported.

max.description: The highest value the source has reported.

avg.description: The average of the values the source has reported.

unit.description: The unit of its values, for people; empty when it has none.

text.description: A text, table or image sensor's text ("" for a table without one); an image sensor's is the reference naming its picture, opaque, 1–2,048 characters, new whenever the picture changes. Absent for a number sensor.

table.description: A table sensor's table; absent for a number, text or image sensor.

history.description: With `?history=n` (n of 1 or more): a number sensor's last n samples at most, oldest first, one every `graphRate` milliseconds (engineSettings; one a second by default, docs/bindings.md#history). Absent otherwise, and for a text, table or image sensor.

status.description: `live`, or `stale` for the last value of a sensor that has stopped updating. A client treats a status it doesn't know as no reading.

sensorTable.description: A table sensor's table in its sensorValue (docs/api.md#fonts-and-sensors): its columns, its first rows, how many rows it has, and the layout its source suggests.

columns.description: Its columns, in order: the names a scene's table input names them by (docs/bindings.md).

rows.description: Its first 10 rows at most, in its order: each a cell's text per column, as a scene's table input reads it.

rowCount.description: How many rows it has, `rows` and the rest.

format.description: The layout its source suggests, as the source gives it (a 1.x table's format: a column's index and width in pixels, pairs joined by `|`, such as `0:200|1:60`); "" when it suggests none.

sensorTableColumn.description: A column of a table sensor's table (sensorTable).

type.description: `number` when its cells are numbers with a unit, each read as text with that unit (`28.6%`), else `text`. A client treats a type it doesn't know as `text`.

unit.description: A number column's unit, the one all its cells have ("%", " MB"); "" for a text column, a number column whose cells differ in unit (" MB" and " GB"), or a table without rows.

sensorSource.description: One sensor source in GET /api/sensors/sources, an array of these: every source the engine runs, in the order it asks them for a key (the order of GET /api/sensors), listed even when it offers no sensors, with its state now and why (docs/api.md#sensor-sources).

id.description: The source's id: the `source` its sensors carry (sensorEntry).

state.description: `starting` (finding its sensors), `running` (reading them), `limited` (reading, but fewer sensors than it could), `unavailable` (it can't read now) or `off` (turned off, or not set up). A client treats a state it doesn't know as `unavailable`.

sensors.description: How many sensors the source lists now (its entries in GET /api/sensors).

driver.description: The Libre source's only (`libre`): the PawnIO driver its sensor helper reads ring0 sensors through (docs/api.md#the-pawnio-driver).

elevation.description: The Libre source's only (`libre`): whether its sensor helper reads every sensor with administrator rights while the engine runs without them (docs/api.md#reading-all-sensors).

libreDriver.description: The PawnIO driver (docs/api.md#the-pawnio-driver): on the Libre source's entry in GET /api/sensors/sources, and the answer to POST /api/sensors/sources/libre/driver.

state.description: `missing` (not installed), `outdated` (older than 2.0, which LibreHardwareMonitor needs), `installed`, `notLoaded` (installed, but the sensor helper can't open it: it runs without administrator rights, or Windows blocked the driver), `installing` (an install the engine started runs now, or ended `installed` and the engine hasn't yet read the driver again and started a new sensor helper for it) or `unknown` (not read: no registry to read, or a sensor helper that doesn't say). A client treats a state it doesn't know as `unknown`.

version.description: The installed version as Windows lists it (dotted whole numbers), or null when the engine doesn't read it or none is installed.

installer.description: The version of the PawnIO installer bundled with the engine that POST /api/sensors/sources/libre/driver runs, or null when there is none (not Windows, a replay, or a build without it).

lastInstall.description: How the last install the engine started since it started ended, or null when none has.

libreDriverInstall.description: How an install of the PawnIO driver ended (docs/api.md#the-pawnio-driver).

outcome.description: `installed`; `restartNeeded` (installed, Windows must restart to finish); `declined` (Windows' prompt for administrator rights was declined: nothing changed); `failed`. A client treats an outcome it doesn't know as `failed`.

code.description: With `failed`: the installer's exit code, when it exited (absent when it couldn't be started).

libreElevation.description: Reading all sensors (docs/api.md#reading-all-sensors): on the Libre source's entry in GET /api/sensors/sources, and the answer to POST and DELETE /api/sensors/sources/libre/elevation.

state.description: `off` (the sensor helper runs with the engine's rights), `on` (a task set up for the engine's user runs it as SYSTEM, so it reads every sensor), `settingUp` (a change the engine started runs now: Windows asks for administrator rights) or `unavailable` (nothing to set up here: `reason` says why). A client treats a state it doesn't know as `unavailable`.

reason.description: With `unavailable` only: `notInstalled` (the engine isn't installed under Program Files, where only administrators write), `notWindows` (another operating system, or a replay) or `engineElevated` (the engine itself runs as administrator, so its sensor helper reads everything already). A client treats a reason it doesn't know as `notInstalled`.

lastChange.description: How the last change the engine started since it started ended, or null when none has.

fallback.description: With `on` only, and only when the sensor helper running is the engine's own instead of the task's: why the last start fell back to it. Codes: `notServing` (the task's helper didn't serve within 10 seconds), `notSystem` (the pipe of its name isn't SYSTEM's), `startRefused` (Windows refused to start the task), `taskUnreadable` (whether the task is set up couldn't be read). A client words the codes it knows and shows `message` for one it doesn't.

libreElevationChange.description: How a change to reading all sensors ended (docs/api.md#reading-all-sensors).

outcome.description: `on` (set up), `off` (removed), `declined` (Windows' prompt for administrator rights was declined: nothing changed) or `failed`. A client treats an outcome it doesn't know as `failed`.

code.description: With `failed`: the sensor helper's exit code, when it exited (absent when it couldn't be started): `10` it didn't get administrator rights, `11` it isn't under Program Files, `12` the engine's user isn't a user of this computer, `13` the Task Scheduler refused, `15` a variable of .NET's couldn't be cleared (the helper wasn't run), `16` its path can't be given to the Task Scheduler as it is; any other is Windows' or the helper's own.

sensorSourceReason.description: Why a source is in its state (docs/api.md#sensor-sources); absent when there is nothing to say.

code.description: The reason for programs, an open code the source names: HWiNFO's `notRunning`, `sharedMemoryOff` and `stopped`; HWiNFO Gadget's `notSetUp`, `notRunning` and `stopped`; Libre's `disabled`, `noDriver`, `driverOutdated`, `driverNotLoaded`, `notElevated` and `helperFailed`; the now-playing source's `helperMissing`, `helperFailed`, `notSupported` and `noSessionBus`; the plugins source's `disabled` (docs/api.md#sensor-sources). A client shows `message` for a code it doesn't know.

message.description: The reason in English, for people.

pluginList.description: GET /api/plugins: whether the engine hosts plugins and every plugin package it found when it started (docs/api.md#plugins).

enabled.description: Whether the engine hosts plugins: false when it was started without them (`--no-plugins`), and then `packages` is empty.

packages.description: The packages the engine found when it started: the bundled ones (beside the engine), then those in its data folder's `plugins/`, each in folder-name order ignoring case.

pluginPackage.description: A plugin package (docs/api.md#plugins): a folder `InfoPanel.{Name}` holding one plugin DLL, run in a host of its own. Never holds a setting's value.

folder.description: The package's folder name, which names it in the requests under /api/plugins/{folder} (matched ignoring case).

name.description: Its name for people: `Name` in its PluginInfo.ini, else its folder name.

version.description: `Version` in its PluginInfo.ini, as written, or null.

website.description: `Website` in its PluginInfo.ini when it is an `http` or `https` URL, else null.

bundled.description: Whether it ships with the engine (beside it, read only) rather than being in the data folder's `plugins/`.

platforms.description: The operating systems its PluginInfo.ini's `Platforms` names, as written, in lower case: `windows`, `macos`, `linux`. Empty: it runs anywhere. A package that doesn't name the engine's (the session's `platform`) is `unsupported`. A client shows a name it doesn't know as given.

on.description: The user's choice: false once turned off (PUT /api/plugins/{folder}/on), kept across restarts. A failure never turns a package off.

state.description: `starting` (its host is starting, or restarting after it ended), `running` (its host runs), `off` (turned off, or not started), `failed` (`reason` says why; its sensors are unavailable until it is reloaded or turned on again) or `unsupported` (it doesn't run on this operating system: no host starts). A client treats a state it doesn't know as `failed`.

reason.description: Why it is `failed` or `unsupported`, or null.

cpu.description: Its host's processor use, in percent of the computer's, as the host last reported it; null until its first report, or while no host runs.

memory.description: Its host's memory in bytes, read by the engine from the host's process: private bytes on Windows, resident size elsewhere; null while no host runs.

sensors.description: How many sensors it lists now (its entries in GET /api/sensors).

plugins.description: The plugins its host loaded this run of the engine (kept once it stops); empty before it has run.

errors.description: Its newest errors, newest first, at most 20: from its plugins, its loads and its host's failures.

pluginReason.description: Why a plugin package is `failed` or `unsupported` (docs/api.md#plugins).

code.description: The reason for programs, an open code: `gaveUp` (its host kept ending, and was restarted as often as the engine restarts one), `notStarted` (its host couldn't be given the folders it writes in), `duplicateId` (it provides a plugin id a package earlier in the list provides) or `platform` (it doesn't run on this operating system). A client words the codes it knows and shows `message` for one it doesn't.

message.description: The reason in English, technical, for people and bug reports.

pluginInfo.description: A plugin a package's host loaded (docs/api.md#plugins).

id.description: The plugin's id: the first part of its sensors' keys (`plugin:/{id}/…`), and its name in the requests under /api/plugins/{folder}/plugins/{id}.

description.description: Its description, for people; empty when it gives none.

sensors.description: How many sensors it lists now.

actions.description: What it can be asked to do (POST /api/plugins/{folder}/plugins/{id}/actions/{method}).

configurable.description: Whether it has settings (GET and PATCH /api/plugins/{folder}/plugins/{id}/settings).

method.description: Its name in the request that runs it.

pluginError.description: An error of a plugin package's, as the engine logged it (a warning).

time.description: When the engine got it: RFC 3339 in UTC with milliseconds, such as "2026-11-06T09:30:00.125Z".

plugin.description: The id of the plugin it came from, or null when it is the package's (its host's, say).

message.description: What it says, technical, for people; never a setting's value.

pluginSwitch.description: PUT /api/plugins/{folder}/on: turns a package on or off.

on.description: True to turn it on (its host is started), false to turn it off (its host is stopped).

pluginSetting.description: One of a plugin's settings, as the plugin answers it: GET and PATCH /api/plugins/{folder}/plugins/{id}/settings answer an array of these (docs/api.md#plugin-settings).

key.description: Its key, which a change names.

description.description: Its description, for people, or null.

type.description: `string` (text, at most 4,096 characters), `integer` (a whole number from −2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647), `number`, `boolean` or `choice` (one of `options`). A client treats a type it doesn't know as one it can't change, and shows its value as given.

value.description: Its value now, as the plugin answers it.

min.description: An `integer`'s or a `number`'s lowest value, when the plugin gives one.

max.description: An `integer`'s or a `number`'s highest value, when the plugin gives one.

step.description: The step a client offers between values, when the plugin gives one; the engine doesn't hold a change to it.

options.description: A `choice`'s options, when the plugin gives them.

key.description: The setting's key, as GET answers it (any length GET lists; the body is held to `requestBytes`).

value.description: Its new value, of the setting's type (pluginSetting).

engineSettings.description: GET /api/settings, and the answer to PATCH /api/settings: the engine settings in effect, each the value set or its default, with how many changes this run made to the stored settings and whether the engine could read them (docs/api.md#settings). `status` tells the two shapes apart: `ok` without a `problem` (engineSettingsOk), or the settings the engine couldn't read with the `problem` (engineSettingsProblem). Read tolerantly: a later engine may add settings, and a client ignores members it doesn't know. A client treats a status it doesn't know as settings it can't change, and shows the `problem` when one comes.

engineSettingsOk.description: The engine read its stored settings (or had none), and they can be changed: no `problem`.

version.description: How many changes this run of the engine made to the stored settings: 0 when it starts, one more after each change that changed them. A value equal to its default is stored, and `null` removes one, so either counts though the value in effect stays the same; a change that leaves the stored settings as they were (the value a setting already has, `null` for one that isn't set, `{}`) doesn't count. It counts within the run the session's and hello's `instance` name, and starts again at 0 when the engine restarts.

frameRate.description: Frames a second for every output without a rate of its own: 1 to 60, 15 by default. The preview socket keeps its own (subscribeMessage's `maxFps`).

graphRate.description: Milliseconds between the samples of the sensor history: 100 to 3000, 1000 by default.

clients.description: Each client's own preferences, by client name, as the client set them: the engine keeps them and never interprets them (docs/api.md#client-preferences). Empty when no client keeps any.

additionalProperties.description: A client's preferences: any JSON value but null.

engineSettingsProblem.description: The engine couldn't read its stored settings when it started: the defaults are in effect, `problem` says why, and every change is refused (409 settingsStatusProblem) until the stored settings are fixed or removed and the engine restarts.

status.description: `unreadable`: the engine couldn't read its stored settings; `unsupported`: they are another major version's. A client treats a status it doesn't know as settings it can't change.

problem.description: Why the engine couldn't read its stored settings, with a JSON pointer into them.

version.description: How many changes this run of the engine made to the stored settings: 0 when it starts, one more after each change that changed them. A value equal to its default is stored, and `null` removes one, so either counts though the value in effect stays the same; a change that leaves the stored settings as they were (the value a setting already has, `null` for one that isn't set, `{}`) doesn't count. It counts within the run the session's and hello's `instance` name, and starts again at 0 when the engine restarts.

frameRate.description: Frames a second for every output without a rate of its own: 1 to 60, 15 by default. The preview socket keeps its own (subscribeMessage's `maxFps`).

graphRate.description: Milliseconds between the samples of the sensor history: 100 to 3000, 1000 by default.

clients.description: Each client's own preferences, by client name, as the client set them: the engine keeps them and never interprets them (docs/api.md#client-preferences). Empty when no client keeps any.

additionalProperties.description: A client's preferences: any JSON value but null.

settingsSources.description: The settings of the engine's sensor sources, by source.

systemInfoSettings.description: The settings of the system information sensor source (`infopanel.system-info`, on macOS and Windows): the processes its tables leave out (docs/api.md#settings). An engine keeps them whether or not it has the source.

excludedProcesses.description: The process names the source's top-process tables (Top CPU Usage, Top CPU Utility, Top Memory Usage) leave out, from its next reading on. A name leaves out the processes of exactly that name: the same case, no white space trimmed, so `node ` or `Node` leaves out no `node`. At most 64 names, each 1 to 64 characters; a name may come twice. By default `_Total`, `Idle`, `dwm`, `csrss`, `svchost`, `lsass`, `system`, `spoolsv` and `Memory Compression`; empty, the tables leave out none.

libreSettings.description: The settings of the LibreHardwareMonitor sensor source (on Windows): whether it reads sensors, whether it reads storage drives, and how often. An engine keeps them whether or not it has the source.

enabled.description: Whether the source reads sensors; true by default.

storage.description: Whether it reads storage drives' sensors; true by default.

storageInterval.description: Seconds between its reads of storage drives: 1 to 300, 30 by default.

networkSettings.description: The settings of the network sensor source (`infopanel.network`, on every operating system): whether it looks up this network's public address. An engine keeps them whether or not it has the source.

publicIp.description: Whether the source asks ipify for this network's public address while a public-address reading is in use, and lists the two (docs/api.md#settings); true by default. Off, it asks nothing and lists neither.

weatherSettings.description: The settings of the weather sensor source (`infopanel.weather`, on every operating system): whether it asks the configured service for the weather, the units it reads in and the place it asks for (docs/api.md#settings). An engine keeps them whether or not it has the source.

enabled.description: Whether the source asks the configured service for the weather; true by default. Off, it asks nothing and its readings are unavailable.

weatherUnits.description: The units the weather source reads in: `auto` (the default: metric, unless the PC's regional format is a region's that uses imperial units), `metric` (°C, hPa, m/s, mm) or `imperial` (°F, inHg, mph, in). A client shows units it doesn't know by their name.

weatherPlace.description: The place the weather source asks for, a place name or `latitude, longitude` in decimal degrees: 1 to 200 characters (UTF-16 code units), not all white space; `null` (the default) asks for the place the service finds for the request's network address.

mediaSettings.description: The settings of the engine's media providers (docs/providers.md).

localNetwork.description: Whether a provider may connect to this computer and the local network (docs/providers.md#addresses); true by default.

renderingSettings.description: Drawing with the GPU (docs/api.md#drawing-with-the-gpu): the setting, and what draws the frames now.

gpu.description: Whether the engine draws its frames with the GPU (Metal on macOS, Direct3D 12 on Windows), read back into the frame every output shares; false by default, the CPU. A change applies from the next frame, without a restart; the GPU failing never changes it.

using.description: What draws the frames now: `cpu`, `metal` or `direct3d12`. A client shows a value it doesn't know as it is.

device.description: The GPU's name while one draws (`using` isn't `cpu`), else null.

fallback.description: Why the CPU draws though `gpu` is true; null otherwise.

renderingFallback.description: Why the CPU draws though `rendering.gpu` is true (docs/api.md#drawing-with-the-gpu).

code.description: `gpu.unsupported`: the engine has no GPU backend on this system. `gpu.noDevice`: no hardware graphics device (none, or only a software one). `gpu.failed`: the device or its context couldn't be made. `gpu.lost`: the device was lost while drawing; turning `gpu` off and on again, or a restart, tries again. A client treats a code it doesn't know as `gpu.failed`.

message.description: What happened, for people: what failed, with the platform's error code where it gives one.

proxySettings.description: The names a reverse proxy on this computer reaches the engine by (docs/api.md#where-requests-come-from).

hosts.description: The names the engine answers besides `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`: a request whose `Host` is one of them, in any case and on any port, is answered as one to a loopback name. Empty by default.

proxyHost.description: A name a reverse proxy on this computer reaches the engine by: a DNS name in lower case, two labels or more, each 1 to 63 of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, neither starting nor ending with `-`, the last starting with a letter (so never an IP address), at most 253 characters, without a trailing dot, a port or a wildcard. An internationalised name is given in its `xn--` form.

logLevel.description: How much the engine logs: the least severe entries it writes to its log, from `debug` (everything) through `information` and `warning` to `error` (errors only). A client shows a level it doesn't know by its name.

clientName.description: A client's name for its preferences (engineSettings' `clients`): 1 to 64 letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens. A client picks a name of its own, such as its product's name in lower case.

settingsChange.description: PATCH /api/settings: the settings to change (docs/api.md#changing-settings). A member given sets that setting, `null` sets it back to its default, and a setting left out keeps its value; `sources`, `sources.libre`, `sources.network`, `sources.weather`, `sources.systemInfo`, `media`, `rendering`, `service`, `proxy` and `clients` are merged member by member, each client's preferences, `proxy.hosts` and `sources.systemInfo.excludedProcesses` set or removed whole. Closed: a member the engine doesn't know is refused. At most `settingsRequestBytes` as received, and the settings it makes are held to the settings limits (docs/limits.md#settings-limits).

excludedProcesses.description: systemInfoSettings: the process names the tables leave out, set whole; `null` sets them back to the default.

gpu.description: renderingSettings: whether the engine draws with the GPU; `null` sets it back to its default, off.

address.description: The configured service's address (serviceSettings): an origin, `https`, or `http` on a loopback host, its scheme and host in any case (the engine keeps it in lower case); `null` sets it back to the engine's default. A change of address removes the credential the engine keeps first, and is refused (503) when it can't (docs/api.md#the-configured-service).

aiApps.description: serviceSettings: whether AI apps elsewhere may use this engine's tools through the configured service; `null` sets it back to its default, off (docs/api.md#ai-apps-elsewhere).

pairing.description: serviceSettings: whether a client on another computer may pair with this engine through a pass the configured service signed; `null` sets it back to its default, off (docs/api.md#pairing-through-the-configured-service).

hosts.description: proxySettings: the names a reverse proxy on this computer reaches the engine by, set whole; `null` sets them back to none. A change applies from the next request.

clients.description: Client preferences to set, each whole, or to remove (`null`), by client name; the other clients' are kept.

additionalProperties.description: A client's preferences: any JSON value, or null to remove them.

settingsStatusProblem.description: 409 application/problem+json to PATCH /api/settings: the engine couldn't read its stored settings when it started (`unreadable`), or they are another major version's (`unsupported`), so it changes none of them until they are fixed or removed and the engine restarts. Nothing was changed.

code.description: The settings' status (engineSettings). A client treats a status it doesn't know as settings it can't change.

serviceSettings.description: The settings of the configured service (docs/api.md#the-configured-service).

aiApps.description: Whether AI apps may use this engine's tools through the configured service (AI apps elsewhere): on, the engine keeps a connection open to the service while it has an address and a credential, and answers the tool calls that arrive over it under its own rules (docs/api.md#ai-apps-elsewhere). Off by default. Only the session token changes it.

pairing.description: Whether a client on another computer may pair with this engine through a pass the configured service signed (pairing through the configured service): on, POST /auth/pairing/pass exchanges a valid pass as POST /auth/pairing/code exchanges a code; off, it refuses every pass (docs/api.md#pairing-through-the-configured-service). Off by default. Only the session token changes it.

serviceAddress.description: The configured service's address in effect: the one set, else the engine's default; null when there is neither (an engine built from source has no default). An origin, `scheme://host[:port]` in lower case without a path: `https`, or `http` on a loopback host (`localhost`, 127.0.0.0/8, `[::1]`).

serviceState.description: GET /api/service: the configured service's address and the state of the credential a client provides for it, never the credential (docs/api.md#the-configured-service). Read tolerantly: a later engine may add members, and a client ignores members it doesn't know.

credential.description: `absent`: the engine keeps no credential; `present`: it keeps one and sends it with its requests to the service; `rejected`: it keeps one the service refused (401), and sends no request to the service until a client provides another. A client treats a value it doesn't know as `absent`.

store.description: Where the engine keeps the credential: `private`, a file in its data folder only this user may read; `protected`, a file in its data folder encrypted for this user by the operating system; `keychain`, the operating system's keychain. Null when `credential` is `absent`. A client shows a value it doesn't know by its name.

fingerprint.description: A fingerprint of the stored credential: the first 16 hexadecimal digits, in lower case, of the SHA-256 of its UTF-8 bytes, so a client can tell which credential the engine keeps without reading it. Null when `credential` is `absent`.

aiApps.description: The connection AI apps elsewhere use (docs/api.md#ai-apps-elsewhere): `off`, none is open or being made (the `service.aiApps` setting is off, or there is no address or no `present` credential to connect with); `connecting`, the engine is connecting, or waiting to connect again after a failure; `connected`, the service accepted the connection; `replaced`, another engine with the same credential took over, and this one stays stopped until the setting is turned off and on again or the engine restarts; `outdated`, the service no longer serves this engine's version, and it stays stopped until the engine is updated; `waiting`, the service asked the engine to wait before connecting again (429), and it will. A client treats a value it doesn't know as `connecting`.

serviceCredential.description: PUT /api/service/credential: a credential a client provides for the configured service, which the engine keeps in place of any it has and sends as `Authorization: Bearer {credential}` (docs/api.md#the-configured-service), and the id the service gave it, which the engine keeps beside it. The credential is an RFC 6750 token: letters, digits, `-`, `.`, `_`, `~`, `+` and `/`, then any `=`, at most 4,096 characters.

id.description: The id the service gave this credential, if it has one: the `device` its pairing passes name (docs/api.md#pairing-through-the-configured-service). 1 to 64 letters, digits, `_` and `-`. Without it, no pass pairs.

serviceProblem.description: application/problem+json to PUT and DELETE /api/service/credential, and to a PATCH /api/settings that changes the service's address: 409 `noService`, the engine has no service address, so it keeps no credential (docs/api.md#the-configured-service); 503 `storeUnavailable`, the store refused to keep or remove it (for a change of address, the credential kept for the old one) and nothing was changed, or it did but couldn't make that durable: then GET /api/service answers what it holds, and a retry finishes it (a change of address stays refused until then). A client treats a code it doesn't know by the status.

status.description: The response's status: 409 or 503. A client treats a status it doesn't know by its class.

code.description: `noService` (409) or `storeUnavailable` (503). A client treats a code it doesn't know by the status.

logPage.description: GET /api/logs: the engine's recent log entries newer than the request's `after`, oldest first, and the `seq` of the newest entry it has logged (docs/api.md#logs). A client polls with `after` set to the `latest` it last read. Read tolerantly: a client ignores members it doesn't know.

entries.description: The kept entries whose `seq` is greater than `after` (every kept entry without it), oldest first: at most the newest 2,000 of the run. When the first one's `seq` isn't `after` + 1, the engine dropped the entries between.

latest.description: The `seq` of the newest entry this run of the engine has logged, kept or not; 0 before the first. It belongs to the run the session's and hello's `instance` name.

logEntry.description: One of the engine's recent log entries, as its log file has it (docs/api.md#logs). `source`, `message` and `exception` are text for people, never a contract: a client shows them and never parses them.

seq.description: The entry's number: 1 for the run's first entry, one more for each entry after it, within the run the session's and hello's `instance` name.

time.description: When it was logged: RFC 3339 with milliseconds and the engine's offset from UTC, such as "2026-10-30T09:30:00.125+08:00".

level.description: How severe it is, from `verbose` through `debug`, `information` and `warning` to `error` and `fatal`. A client treats a level it doesn't know as `information`.

source.description: The part of the engine that logged it, for people, or empty; one longer than 256 characters is cut, ending in "…".

message.description: What it says, for people; one longer than 4,096 characters is cut, ending in "…".

exception.description: The error it records, as text for people, when there is one; one longer than 8,192 characters is cut, ending in "…".

displayList.description: GET /api/displays: the displays of the computer the engine runs on, read when the request came (docs/api.md#displays). Read tolerantly: a client ignores members it doesn't know.

supported.description: Whether this engine shows desktop windows, and so can list the displays. When false, `displays` is empty: a client tells "no displays" (true, and empty) from "this engine can't list them".

displays.description: The displays, the primary one first, then in the order the system gives them.

displayInfo.description: One display (docs/api.md#displays). `id`, `name`, `width`, `height`, `x` and `y` are exactly the `displayMatch` a profile's `window.display` takes to put its window on this display (urn:infopanel:document:1#/$defs/displayMatch).

id.description: The monitor's identity from its EDID, its PNP maker and product code (`DEL40F4`); absent when the display reports none (a virtual or remote display, an adapter that hides the EDID, an engine that doesn't read it).

name.description: The name the engine matches the display by, at most 256 characters (a longer one is cut).

width.description: The display's width in its own pixels.

height.description: The display's height in its own pixels.

x.description: The display's left edge in the desktop's own coordinates (points on macOS, not pixels on a scaled display; pixels on Windows).

y.description: The display's top edge in the desktop's own coordinates (points on macOS, not pixels on a scaled display; pixels on Windows).

label.description: The display's name for people, at most 256 characters (a longer one is cut): the same as `name` where the system has one name for it, else the name the system shows people.

scale.description: The display's pixels per unit of the desktop's own coordinates (2 on a Retina display on macOS; 1 on Windows, whose desktop coordinates are pixels).

primary.description: Whether it is the primary display (the main one, where a window without `display` goes). Only the first display listed is.

deviceList.description: GET /api/devices: the USB panels the engine has saved, in the order it first saw them, and their state now (docs/api.md#devices). Read tolerantly: a client ignores members it doesn't know.

supported.description: Whether the engine drives USB panels this run. When false, `devices` is empty and `reason` says why.

reason.description: Why `supported` is false, else null: `off` (the engine was started without panels), `library` (it has no USB library) or `store` (it couldn't read its devices file when it started: it changes no device this run and leaves the file as it is). A client treats a reason it doesn't know as `library`.

oneOf.description: A client treats a reason it doesn't know as `library`.

version.description: How many times the list has changed in this run of the engine (the `devices` message's): 0 when it starts, greater for a later change. A change of the running panels' `stats` alone counts at most once a second.

families.description: Every panel family the engine knows this run: its built-in families, then those its panel packages declare (bundled ones first, then those in its data folder's `plugins/`, each in folder-name order), whether their package is on, off or failed; empty when `supported` is false. Absent from an engine without panel packages: a client then knows only the families it knows itself.

detected.description: The USB devices plugged in now that look like a panel of a family the engine knows but that no family drives (docs/api.md#detected-devices), in the order the system lists them, at most 64. Detection reads only the descriptors the USB stack has already cached; it never opens, claims or sends anything to a detected device. (Listing USB devices at all goes through libusb's enumeration, which on some systems reads a new device's descriptors once, as it does for every panel family.) Absent when `supported` is false, and from an engine that doesn't list them.

deviceDetected.description: A USB device that looks like a panel of a family the engine knows (one of the family's detect patterns names its ids) but that no family drives, as the system's cached descriptors give it (docs/api.md#detected-devices).

family.description: The family whose patterns name it, as deviceFamily.id names it.

usb.description: Its USB vendor and product ids, four lower-case hexadecimal digits each, as "4e58:1002".

port.description: The USB port path it is plugged in at, as the system numbers it ("0-1.2").

bcdDevice.description: Its release number as its device descriptor gives it, binary-coded decimal (256 is 1.00).

interfaces.description: Its interfaces (each one's first alternate setting) in its active configuration, else its first, at most 32.

deviceDetectedInterface.description: An interface of a detected device: its class codes and endpoints.

endpoints.description: Its endpoints but endpoint 0, at most 30.

deviceDetectedEndpoint.description: An endpoint of a detected device's interface.

address.description: Its bEndpointAddress: its number, with 128 added for an in endpoint (129 is endpoint 1 in).

type.description: Its transfer type: `control`, `isochronous`, `bulk` or `interrupt`. A client shows a type it doesn't know as it is.

maxPacketSize.description: The largest packet it takes, in bytes.

deviceFamily.description: A panel family the engine knows (docs/api.md#panel-families): built in, or declared by a panel package's panel.json.

id.description: The family's id, as deviceEntry.family and createDeviceRequest.family name it: a lower-case letter, then at most 31 letters and digits.

name.description: Its name for people: a built-in family's is the engine's English (a client words the families it knows itself), a package's is its panel.json's.

driver.description: `builtIn`, or the folder name of the panel package that declares it (`InfoPanel.{Name}`).

state.description: `ready` (built in, or its package is on: its host runs while a panel of it is plugged in), `off` (its package is turned off: its panels are `off` with the `driver` reason) or `failed` (its package can't run, `reason` says why: its panels are `failed` with the `driver` reason). A client treats a state it doesn't know as `failed`.

reason.description: Why it is `failed`, else null: `code` (`gaveUp`: its package's host kept ending and was restarted as often as the engine restarts one, three times in a minute; `sdk`: its package is built for a panel SDK this engine doesn't have; the codes are open) and `message`.

models.description: Its models, as its package declares them (a built-in family's, the engine's), at most 512.

supports.description: The settings its panels honour, as deviceEntry.supports names them.

transports.description: How its panels are reached, each once: `usb` (USB transfers), `serial` (a USB serial port) or `hid` (HID reports).

items.description: A client treats a transport it doesn't know as `usb`.

settings.description: The settings of its own its panels take, as its package's panel.json declares them, in its order (docs/api.md#family-settings); absent when it declares none.

deviceFamilySetting.description: A setting a panel family declares for its panels (docs/api.md#family-settings): a panel's value is in deviceEntry.familySettings, changed through deviceChange.familySettings.

id.description: Its key in a panel's familySettings.
